result.title: Regime-Aware Router Learning for Multi-Domain Medical Image Generation with Diffusion Experts
result.summary: Heterogeneous medical image data motivate domain-specialized diffusion experts, but expert specialization alone does not determine how their predictions should be combined during sampling. Learning a global router is particularly challenging when the server has limited, potentially unrepresentative images. We study two router-learning strategies for a fixed expert pool. Server-Only learns input- and timestep-dependent expert assignments from server images with component labels. Anchor-Delta (AD) uses the same images and frozen experts to obtain additional evidence from denoising losses. It distills targets that combine this evidence with the current router's assignments, while a proxy gate controls a subsequent refinement step. Component labels describe data origin; expert losses measure empirical prediction performance. We evaluate these distinct signals through routing analyses and paired medical image generation. An AD-trained router improves generation metrics over Server-Only in a heterogeneous four-domain setting, and a separate server-data study shows gains in held-out routing over a corrected-routing comparator. Additional paired evaluations show that the effect of inference-time evidence mixing varies across benchmarks. These findings establish server-data availability and expert performance as distinct considerations in learning routers for multi-domain diffusion models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在固定 diffusion expert 池上如何学习组合专家的路由器：比较仅用服务器图像与分量标签的 Server-Only 策略，以及借助去噪损失蒸馏路由目标、并用代理门控后续精修的 Anchor-Delta，在异构四域医学图像生成上评估路由与生成效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按输入与时间步分配专家、并以专家去噪损失作为性能证据来蒸馏路由目标的做法，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态更新的贡献分配、无真值标签下的监督信号来源有可供核查的迁移线索；但属图像生成路由场景，联系需人工判断。
